Baseline projections indicate that Lodge Grass will have a substantial, although gradual, increase in population over the next 25 years, primarily as a result of natural increase in Crow population. The additional population will increase demand for city services and will strain the city's ability to provide adequate services. Lodge Grass is beginning to investigate outside sources of revenue to relieve some of the existing pressures. The town recently received a $100,000 grant from the Department of Housing and Urban Development (H.U.D.) to replace the water pipes in a six-block area. The town clerk feels that much more aid is needed, especially for water system improvements, because the town cannot raise the mill levy and little increase in taxable valuation is foreseen (George Lix, Town Clerk, personal communication, January 7, 1976).
For the city of Hardin, expenditures have increased at a much more rapid rate than have revenues. The revenues cannot be increased now except through increases in taxable value. Some increase in taxable value is foreseen because property within the city is being reevaluated for the first time since 1964 (Big Horn County Appraiser, personal communication, January 8, 1976). The reevaluation is based on replacement costs and will double the taxable value for some property. The reevaluation is being completed in steps and will end with dwellings in 1977 or 1978. In future years, evaluation will not fall as far behind because the 1975 legislature passed a bill requiring 20 percent of all property to be reevaluated each year.
